metadata.description: `<out>/.vibe-site/state.json` — what the registry builder has rendered, and what it rendered it from (PROP-057 `##SITE-RENDER-KEY`, campaign atom A5.2). It is the ONE thing that makes a second run cheap: the builder reads the index, compares the content hash of each published version with the hash it rendered that version from, and queues only what moved. It is not a history and cannot become one — there is exactly one row per coordinate and version, holding the CURRENT render, because a version number may be published many times and only the last publication exists, in the registry as on the site (`##SITE-VERSION-SHOWS-CURRENT`, §14). Nothing in it reaches a reader: the render key is the builder's, never a page's. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_site_state/`.

One row per rendered coordinate and version, sorted so two runs over an unchanged site write the same bytes. An empty list is a builder that has rendered nothing yet, which is what the first run of a fresh output directory reads.

When the host half last completed. The debounce of `##SITE-HOST-POLL` is measured from here and not from each row, because the host is polled as one source: a branch that moves ten times an hour must not cost ten renders, and the rows it produced all became current together. Absent until the first host render completes.
One version, as it stands in the output now.

Where this version came from: the alias of the `[[source.registry]]` that published it, or the host's repository when it came from the checkout. Provenance and not identity — the row is keyed by the coordinate and the version — so that a report can say which feed a queued rebuild came from.

The hash of the bytes this render was made from: the index's `content_hash` for a registry package, and a recomputation over the files it reads for the host's checkout, whose in-tree packages keep their version number while their content moves (`##SITE-RENDER-KEY`). It is the render key and nothing else — never shown to a reader, never an address, never compared against anything but the current source.
How many files the render wrote. A number a report can print and a second run can compare, and the cheapest signal that a render which claimed success produced nothing.

True when the render did not succeed and the address carries a «render failed» page instead (`##SITE-RENDER-IDEMPOTENT`). A failed row is re-queued on the next run even when the source has not moved: leaving it alone would make one bad package permanent, since nothing about it will ever change to trigger a rebuild.
